newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO no comment on TV fraud programme.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO no comment on TV fraud programme.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Monday it had no comment on a television programme due to be aired tonight dealing with a 25 million guilder fraud allegedly committed against the bank by one of its staff.

Spokesman Jules Prast said the bank understood the programme to be screened on the RTL4 station at 2000 GMT would focus on the case of a 29 year old Turkish man arrested in July on suspicion of transferring funds to accounts in Abu Dubai in the United Arab Emirates.
The man allegedly withdrew money in June from accounts of the bank's corporate clients, who have since been compensated by ABN AMRO.
"We never comment on cases that are before the public prosecutors' office," Prast told Reuters.
Prast added that although the bank believed a fraud had been committed, "that does not mean that the computer system is not okay".
He said ABN AMRO staff had been told of the programme in an internal communication, to prepare them for any questions that clients might ask after watching it.
